docs.title: ANNIE Data and MC Samples
docs.text:
Where to find ANNIE's production data and simulation samples, which ones to use, and how to ask for new ones.

New to ANNIE data?

Start with Getting started and the technote Preparing Data for Analysis (DocDB 6699).

docs.text: If you need Use Status Beam data to develop an analysis Gen 1 2% unblinded subset Recommended Beam data for a final analysis Gen 1 ProcessedData and BeamClusterTrees (blinded) Recommended Neutrino interactions in the tank Gen 1 MC central value: tank Recommended Neutrino interactions in the whole geometry Gen 1 MC central value: world Recommended MC with untilted PMTs (detector variation) Untilted PMTs Available The newest processing Gen 2 data In production

docs.title: How this site is organised
docs.text:
• Samples are grouped by generation: one consistent processing of the data, plus the MC meant to be compared with it.
    • Generation 1: FY22–FY25 data event-built with EBV2. This is the data in the current publications and theses.
    • Generation 2: reprocessing with ToolAnalysis V1.6.0, starting with FY25.
  • Every sample has a status label. The labels are explained in Getting started.
  • Samples are given as dCache paths. SAM definitions will be added later.
  • Superseded samples are on the Deprecated page, with the reason for each.

docs.title: Requesting a sample
docs.text: Requests are GitHub issues made from a form: open a request. The forms and what happens next are described on Requesting a sample.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: The site is written in Markdown in ANNIEsoft/ANNIE_Samples, built with Material for MkDocs, and published by GitHub Actions on every push to main.

docs.title: Small fixes
docs.text: Click the pencil icon at the top of a page, edit the file on GitHub, and propose the change as a pull request.

docs.title: Adding a sample
docs.text:
Copy this block into the right page and fill it in. Give the heading an explicit { #id } so links to it keep working if the title changes.

### Sample name { #sample-id }

<span class="badge recommended">Recommended</span>

One or two sentences: what the sample is and what it is for. Caveats, if any.

| Stage | Software | Path |
|---|---|---|
| GENIE | GENIE v3.0.6, G18_10a_02_11a | `/pnfs/annie/persistent/...` |
| WCSim, PMT | WCSim v2.0.0-ANNIE, CC tuning | `/pnfs/annie/persistent/...` |

**Events / POT:** ... · **Contact:** ... · **Request:** [#N](https://github.com/ANNIEsoft/ANNIE_Samples/issues/N)

Status badges (meanings in Getting started):

<span class="badge recommended">Recommended</span>
<span class="badge available">Available</span>
<span class="badge analysis">Analysis-specific</span>
<span class="badge production">In production</span>
<span class="badge planned">Planned</span>
<span class="badge dq">DQ only</span>
<span class="badge deprecated">Deprecated</span>

When a sample is superseded, move its entry to Deprecated and add a line saying why and what replaces it.

docs.title: Previewing locally
docs.text:
python3 -m pip install --user -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ANNIE_Samples/ (the path matches the published site's URL). mkdocs build --strict fails on broken links, as the pull-request check does.

docs.title: Before you analyse data
docs.text:
The reference is the technote Preparing Data for Analysis (S. Doran, DocDB 6699). In short:

  1. Start from an existing processed sample. Re-process raw data only if your analysis needs a different event building or reconstruction.
  2. Follow the blinding scheme. Develop on MC first. The 2% unblinded subset is the first look at data in the signal region.
  3. Select good-beam triggers: the undelayed beam trigger, horn current, toroid range and agreement, and a paired PMT timestamp. Where needed, also require bunch rotation off, a good BRF fit, and the extended-readout mode you want. The cut values are in the technote.
  4. Compute POT from the triggers you selected, with one toroid (TOR860 is the usual choice). The run-period POT is for planning only.
  5. MC and data use different timing references. Do not copy an absolute hitT cut from MC to data.
  6. Off-beam triggers have no MRD or FMV data. If your selection needs them, use the pre-beam window to estimate beam-uncorrelated backgrounds.

docs.title: Blinding
docs.text:
ANNIE analyses look at data in stages. The scheme written for the first νμ CC analysis (J. Minock and A. Mastbaum, Blindness Scheme for ANNIE CC Analysis, DocDB 6259) is the model:

  1. MC only. Develop the whole analysis on the GENIE central value: signal definition, selection, observables and binning, POT normalisation, systematics, unfolding.
  2. Data sidebands. Check the analysis on control regions outside the signal region, filtered from the full data.
  3. 2% of the data. The first look at the signal region, using the 2% unblinded subset. This is the last chance to change the analysis.
  4. 10% of the data. A final check before full unblinding.
  5. Full data.

The results of each stage are shown to the collaboration before moving to the next. Analyses with neutrons, other final states or other detector configurations may need their own version of the scheme.

Analysis coordinators: Jingbo Wang (jingbo.wang@sdsmt.edu) and Andy Mastbaum (mastbaum@physics.rutgers.edu). Contact them before accessing blinded data.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: ProcessedData Event-built data: ToolAnalysis BoostStores with the PMT, MRD, LAPPD, trigger and beam information of each event, one directory of part files per run. Beam information (POT per trigger) is stored with each event. BeamClusterTrees (BeamCluster ntuples) ROOT ntuples made from ProcessedData by the BeamClusterAnalysis toolchain (ANNIEEvent tree Event): event, trigger, beam, PMT-cluster and MRD information. EBV2 Event building version 2 (Yue Feng, DocDB 6043). Generation (Gen 1, Gen 2) One consistent processing of the data, and the MC meant to be compared with it. ghep, gst GENIE output: the full event record (ghep) and the flat summary tree (gst). anniedirt (g4dirt) Geant4 propagation of the GENIE final state through the rock and hall to the detector. WCSim pmt and lappd files WCSim writes the PMT and LAPPD responses to separate files. CC tuning, NC tuning The two WCSim detector-response tunings. See Gen 1 MC. SANDI A water-based liquid scintillator (WbLS) target in the tank, deployed in SANDI I (Mar–May 2023; see JINST 19 P05070) and SANDI II (Nov 2024–Feb 2025). Do not use those runs unless you are doing a WbLS analysis. TOR860, TOR875 The two BNB toroids that measure protons on target (POT). They agree to within a few percent.

docs.title: Status labels
docs.text: Label Meaning Recommended The default choice for its purpose. Available Valid and documented, but not the default. Analysis-specific Made for one analysis, often in a personal area. Check with the contact before relying on it. In production Being produced. Paths and contents may change. Planned Not produced yet. DQ only Data-quality processing. Not for final analyses. Deprecated Superseded and kept for reproducibility. Listed on Deprecated.

docs.title: Requesting a sample
docs.text:
Requests are GitHub issues made from a form (you need a GitHub account). Open a request and pick the form that fits:

Form Label Use it for MC sample request MC New simulation: GENIE, anniedirt, WCSim, MC ntuples, particle guns, cosmics Fake-data request FakeData Samples from an alternative model or generator, or reweighted samples, used as fake data Data sample request Data Special data processing: calibration samples, run selections, reprocessing, filtered ntuples Report a problem with a sample sample-problem A wrong path, missing or broken files, or a wrong description on this site

docs.title: Before you ask
docs.text:
• Check the recommended samples: an existing sample may already do.
  • dCache space is shared by all of ANNIE. A full MC production (4000 runs, all stages) takes about 0.4 TB. Ask for what you need.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
1. A new request gets the label status: new.
  2. The maintainers review it and set status: approved or status: declined (with the reason).
  3. While it is being made: status: in production.
  4. When it is ready, a pull request adds the sample to this site and closes the issue, so every sample links back to its request.

docs.title: Run periods
docs.text:
Beam data from FY22 onward can be event-built. Earlier data used a different DAQ configuration and currently cannot be.

Period ANNIE run Dates DAQ runs ≈ POT (TOR860) In Gen 1 Notes FY22 3 (partial) Jan–Jul 2022 3207–3844 2.04e20 yes single LAPPD FY23 SANDI I 4 Mar–May 2023 4208–4314 0.51e20 yes, own subset WbLS target (JINST 19 P05070): do not use unless doing WbLS FY23 rest 4 Dec 2022–Jul 2023 4001–4207, 4315–4450 1.75e20 yes mostly single LAPPD FY24 MRD stable 5 Feb–May 2024 4725–4809 0.49e20 yes multi-LAPPD FY24 MRD rack 8 fault 5 May–Jul 2024 4810–4965 0.85e20 no limited MRD and FMV performance FY25 SANDI II 6 Nov 2024–Feb 2025 5081–5328 0.88e20 yes, own subset WbLS target: do not use unless doing WbLS FY25 rest 6 Feb–Jul 2025 5329–5668 2.65e20 yes multi-LAPPD FY26 7 — — — no (Gen 2) PMTs repaired in Dec 2025: "golden" data from Jan 2026 FY27 — taking data now — — no (Gen 2) repaired PMTs

Fiscal-year totals: FY22 2.04e20, FY23 2.26e20, FY24 1.34e20, FY25 3.53e20. Generation 1 holds about 8.3e20 POT, 6.9e20 of it without SANDI.

PMT configuration

From FY22 until the PMT repairs in December 2025 the WB and Watchman PMTs were tilted, so all Generation 1 data has tilted PMTs, as does the Gen 1 MC central value. Data from January 2026 onward (midway through FY26) has the repaired PMTs, and the MC has not been tuned for it.

Extended readout, FY23

About 40 runs between 4191 and 4410 (in both SANDI I and the rest of FY23) have almost no extended readout (rate below 10⁻³). See DocDB 5166.

The per-run list (fiscal year, TOR860 POT, SANDI, MRD rack 8 fault and extended-readout flags) is attached to the Summer 2026 data-quality talk (S. Doran). Runs with fewer than three part files are left out of it.

docs.title: POT
docs.text:
The POT above is approximate: it comes from CTC-recorded beam triggers and is meant for planning. Report the POT of an analysis from the events you selected. POT per trigger is stored with each event in the ProcessedData BoostStore and in the BeamCluster ntuples (beam_E_TOR860, beam_pot_875). Use one toroid throughout and say which. TOR860 is the usual choice (MicroBooNE and the ANNIE CC and NC analyses).

Resource Where POT tables by run, FY23 DocDB 5607 POT tables by run, FY24 DocDB 5604 POT tables by run, FY25 DocDB 6198 Good-beam POT and trigger counts by run, FY22–FY23 (NCQE run selection) POT_trigger_FY22_23_summary.csv Beam-device and POT files, one per run (beamfetcher_<run>.root) /pnfs/annie/persistent/processed/BeamFetcherV2

docs.title: How many events?
docs.text: For a rough size estimate: FY22–FY23 recorded about 2.4e5 triggers per 1e18 POT (all trigger types). In the NCQE run selection, that is about 4.1e7 triggers in 1.8e20 POT for FY22, and 2.0e7 triggers in 0.82e20 POT for FY23. Other years may differ.

docs.title: Generation 1: Data
docs.text:
Generation 1 is the FY22–FY25 beam data event-built with EBV2 by Yue Feng and Steven Doran, using fengyvoid/ToolAnalysis v1.1 run through autoANNIE. It is the data behind the CC-inclusive, CC0π, MicroBooNE–ANNIE CC0π joint, NCQE and first LAPPD (JINST 21 P02002) analyses, and the theses of Steven Doran (DocDB 6712), James Minock (DocDB 6976) and Yue Feng (DocDB 6705).

It covers FY22, FY23 (including SANDI I), FY24 runs 4725–4809 (MRD stable), and FY25 (including SANDI II): about 8.3e20 POT. See Run periods and POT.

Blinded data

The full Generation 1 ProcessedData and BeamClusterTrees are blinded. Please contact the analysis coordinators, Jingbo Wang and Andy Mastbaum, before accessing them, and follow the blinding scheme.

SANDI runs

SANDI I (runs 4208–4314; JINST 19 P05070) and SANDI II (runs 5081–5328) had a WbLS target in the tank. Do not use them unless you are doing a WbLS analysis.

docs.title: Generation 1: MC
docs.text:
The simulation chain is BNB flux (gsimple) → GENIE → anniedirt → WCSim → MC ntuples (ToolAnalysis). New productions use ANNIE_MC_Production.

Central productions live under /pnfs/annie/persistent/simulations/<software>/G1810a0211a/<production>/<volume>/, where <software> is genie3, g4dirt (anniedirt) or wcsim, and WCSim adds a pmt/ or lappd/ level.

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Stage Repository Version GENIE ANNIEsoft/GENIE-v3 GENIE v3.0.6, tune G18_10a_02_11a anniedirt ANNIEsoft/anniedirt branch genie_3_0_6 (container image anniesoft/g4dirt:latest) WCSim ANNIEsoft/WCSim v2.0.0-ANNIE, v2.1.0-ANNIE WCSim, NC tuning S81D/WCSim not yet merged into ANNIEsoft/WCSim

anniedirt carries the GENIE final-state particles through the rock and hall until they reach the tank water or another detector volume (MRD, FMV). Only those events go on to WCSim: for world samples that is about 650 of the 20,000 events in each GENIE file, for tank samples nearly all of them.

docs.title: PMT configuration and tunings
docs.text:
From FY22 until the PMT repairs in December 2025, the WB and Watchman PMTs were tilted. In WCSim this is modelled as a 53° tilt from the panel normal plus a 13.9 cm upward shift along the tank height.

The MC has only been tuned for the tilted configuration, so the tilted geometry is the central value. Before the tilt was found, the MC assumed untilted PMTs. Because the tilt in the simulation is only approximate, that untilted geometry is kept as a detector variation.

Data after the PMT repairs

Data from January 2026 onward (midway through FY26) has the repaired PMTs. The MC has not been tuned for it.

Tuning WCSim settings Code CC tuning QE ratio 1.025 set in WCSim; parametric PMT model ANNIEsoft/WCSim v2.0.0-ANNIE, v2.1.0-ANNIE NC tuning PMT waveform simulation; PMT collection efficiency; QE ratio 1.50 S81D/WCSim (not yet merged into ANNIEsoft/WCSim)

Unless a sample says otherwise, WCSim uses the Geant4 physics list FTFP_BERT_HP with the ANNRI neutron-capture model.

The tuning to through-going muons and Michel electrons is described in MC Tuning and Validation (S. Doran, DocDB 5962). ANNIE's WCSim has diverged from upstream WCSim: its tags start at v2.0.0-ANNIE, and earlier tags in the repository are upstream's.

docs.title: Central value (CC tuning)
docs.text:
GENIE v3.0.6 with tune G18_10a_02_11a (ANNIEsoft/GENIE-v3) and anniedirt, both from the standardv1.0 production, then WCSim v2.1.0-ANNIE with the tilted and shifted PMTs and the CC tuning. Each GENIE file has 20,000 events drawn from 50 randomly chosen flux files, which gives smooth true-energy spectra. The older standard production drew each file from a single flux file and is deprecated.

POT normalisation

GENIE stores the POT of each file as the weight of its gtree tree (gtree->GetWeight() in the ghep file; see pot_from_ghep.py). Normalise by summing it over the GENIE files behind the WCSim files you use. The per-event numbers below are for estimates only.

WCSim version

The WCSim directory is called standardv2.0.0_tilt_shift, but it was made with WCSim v2.1.0-ANNIE. It also holds test samples for Yue Feng's LAPPD modifications.

docs.title: NC-tuned samples
docs.text: Samples made for the NCQE analysis with the NC tuning: world volume, tilted and shifted PMTs, PMT files only, unless stated otherwise. Contact: Steven Doran.

docs.title: NC tuning: GENIE-Base
docs.text:
Analysis-specific

A separate GENIE and anniedirt production with the same GENIE build and configuration as the central value: statistically independent, but otherwise nearly identical. Simulated in WCSim with both the NC and the CC tuning.

docs.title: Generation 2: Data
docs.text:
In production

Generation 2 reprocesses the data with ANNIEsoft/ToolAnalysis V1.6.0, with the updated event building described in Decoder stage (Anuj Gupta, DocDB 7006). FY25 is being processed first. FY22–FY24, FY26 and FY27 (being taken now) will follow, and there will be a Generation 2 2% unblinded subset.

Blinded data

Generation 2 beam data is blinded. Please contact the analysis coordinators, Jingbo Wang and Andy Mastbaum, before accessing it, and follow the blinding scheme.
